questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Finding off-campus housing in Hong Kong was definitely a mixed bag. I ended up in Sham Shui Po, and while it’s a real cultural hub, it felt a little sketchy at times. I had to be super careful about avoiding scams since a lot of landlords target international students. I even had my bank look over the contract to make sure it was legit!

For anyone looking for a place, I'd say stick to well-known websites like roomgo. Those listings are usually safer. Also, my uni had some resources and Facebook groups where students shared leads on apartments. Super helpful!

If you’re looking for other neighborhoods, maybe check out places like Kowloon Tong or in general Hong Kong island. They feel a bit safer, and there are more options. Just keep your wits about you, and don't rush into anything.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer:
Get familiar with wet market! These are local markets where you can find fresh produce, meats, and seafood. They have a super lively atmosphere and are a great way to immerse yourself in the local culture. Plus, shopping there is usually way cheaper than at
supermarkets.Next
, be cautious about overpaying just because you’re a foreigner. Some vendors might mark up prices for non-locals. When you’re checking out a new place, take a moment to look around and get a feel for average prices before you buy. It’s a good idea to ask local friends or fellow students about fair prices for food or basic goods; they can help you spot inflated prices.
Learning a couple of basic Cantonese phrases can also go a long way. Simple greetings or phrases like “How much?” (几多钱? - gei do qian?) can make a difference in how you’re treated and help you blend in more.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
The registration process at my host institution in Hong Kong was relatively straightforward, but it did involve several steps to ensure everything was in order for my exchange semester. Here’s how it generally went (as I remember):

Pre-Arrival Preparation: Before arriving, I had to complete an online pre-registration form provided by the university. This form included my personal details, program information, and any course preferences I had. I was also required to submit my proof of enrollment and some supporting documents, like a copy of my passport and visa.

Course Registration: After orientation, I logged into the university’s online course registration system. I had to select and enroll in my courses based on the availability and prerequisites. The system had a clear interface, but it was crucial to act fast since some classes filled up quickly! I also consulted the academic advisor regarding course loads and requirements, which provided clarity.

Submitting Documents: Once I had my classes sorted out, I had to submit some additional documents, such as health insurance proof and a completed registration form detailing my chosen courses. This was done both online and in-person at the international office.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: There are advisors to reach out to from both your faculty and from student-support networks.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer:
Unfortunately, my experience with registering for the classes I wanted wasn't very successful. When I logged into the online course registration system, I found that there had been some discrepancies in the course catalog. Some of the classes I initially intended to enroll in weren't available, as the catalog had outdated information. This caused quite a bit of confusion and frustration.

As a result, I ended up having to choose elective courses instead of my preferred options. While some of the electives turned out to be interesting, it wasn’t what I had set out to study. I reached out to the academic advisor to discuss my options, but by then, many of the popular courses were already full.

Overall, I learned the importance of being flexible and adaptable in such situations, but it was disappointing not to get into the classes that aligned with my academic goals. I would recommend future students to double-check course availability ahead of time and have backup options ready, just in case any issues arise with the registration process.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Do not hesitate with reaching out to some of the outreach-resources

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I would say my satisfaction with the academic program at my host institution was somewhat mixed. While the course content was interesting and offered valuable insights, the assessment methods primarily focused on testing rote memorization of course material rather than fostering critical thinking or applying knowledge to real-life situations. 

Many exams and assignments required us to recall information without much emphasis on analysis or practical application. This approach felt limiting at times, as I prefer learning environments that challenge me to think critically and engage with the material in a meaningful way.

I did appreciate the quality of some professors, who were knowledgeable and approachable, but I found myself craving more opportunities for discussion, projects, and real-world applications of the concepts we were learning. I believe that an academic program should aim to equip students with skills that extend beyond traditional testing, especially in today's rapidly changing world.

Overall, while there were strong elements within the program, I would encourage future exchange students to seek courses that not only interest them but also prioritize critical thinking and practical application, as those aspects can significantly enhance the overall learning experience.
